title: The first press of play on a long recording does not hitch
goal: On a five minute recording, the first time you press play the window stops answering for about a sixth of a second before the picture moves. Later presses are fine. A press should never hold the window that long.
notes: Found while fixing starting-an-export-does-not-freeze-the-window. Repro (temp walk: openLongRetinaTalk, wait 1.5, videoPause, wait 0.6, key l, wait 0.5, key k, wait 0.3, key l, wait 0.5, key k): Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/exstall/lonly.json --no-build, run twice. Output: first L wait -> "0.5s, never went quiet (14 of 14 slices busy); mainBusy 410.6ms over 269 passes, longest 156.7ms" and "... longest 149.3ms"; second L -> longest 34.6ms / 22.0ms. During an export the same first press read longest 67.4ms. Not yet sampled: run sample(1) on the probe across the first L to find the long pass.
acceptance: On the five minute Retina sample, the first L press after opening keeps the longest main thread stretch under 50 ms (today about 150 ms)
The cause is named in the task log with the measurement that shows it
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on
